items.title: Welcome by the School Board President
Discussion Items – Review of Preliminary Ideas Generated by North Star Forward Committee

publicComments.name: David Weekley
publicComments.summary: Urged the board to keep students at the center of this process, ensuring North Star changes if it harms any students and that the focus remains on maximizing the potential of every student in the district.

publicComments.name: Lily Milton
publicComments.summary: Speaking as a North Star Forward Committee member and Orion parent, she expressed appreciation for the process and presented the subcommittee's key recommendations: changing grade configuration so North Star no longer begins at third grade, and bringing compacted curriculum and enrichment to all schools, while urging the board to act with urgency on broader equity issues.

publicComments.name: Unidentified speaker
publicComments.summary: Argued that the Bayside access data is misleading since many Bayside families already access North Star via school of choice, that North Star is not broken and serves its community at no extra cost, and urged the board to focus on the 70% of students who are academically behind rather than restructuring a well-designed school.

publicComments.name: John Kinsel
publicComments.summary: Expressed strong support for North Star as a program that keeps academically advanced students engaged and challenged, and suggested the real focus should be on improving conditions at other schools rather than changing North Star.

publicComments.name: Owen Webel
publicComments.summary: As a North Star graduate, shared that his previous school left him disengaged due to lack of challenge, while North Star allowed him to make friends at his own level and progress further academically.

publicComments.name: Tony Webel
publicComments.summary: As a North Star committee member and parent of children at both Roosevelt and North Star, he emphasized that the primary objective should be the best equitable learning environment for all students, and raised concerns that some committee ideas conflict with that goal, also requesting the Jamboard document be removed from materials as rushed and misleading.

publicComments.name: Jessica Nodi
publicComments.summary: As a Roy Cloud parent and educator, expressed support for starting North Star at kindergarten, bringing the enrichment model to all students at all sites, and offering equal enrollment percentages from all schools.

publicComments.name: Katie Morello
publicComments.summary: As a Henry Ford parent, described the emotional impact on her daughter losing 15 classmates and suggested that if North Star is a strong accelerated school, middle school might be a more appropriate entry point.

publicComments.name: Kaylee Vega
publicComments.summary: As a Henry Ford parent who chose the district partly because of North Star, argued that North Star is not the problem and that the other district schools being under-resourced and underperforming is the real issue, urging the board not to dismantle a highly ranked program.

publicComments.name: Loan Hin
publicComments.summary: As a Henry Ford parent who personally benefited from a magnet school as a child, stated her family would leave the district if North Star is not available at third grade, and argued that equity and access issues can be addressed without eliminating the North Star format.

publicComments.name: Elle Kolekar
publicComments.summary: As a Bayside family with children attending Hillside schools including North Star, argued that the equity problem is a deeper district-wide issue not caused solely by North Star, and called on the board to invest in and strengthen Bayside community schools.

publicComments.name: Alice Harkey
publicComments.summary: As North Star's parent club president, described the transformational impact of North Star on her children, expressed support for universal testing and expanded outreach including busing and after-school support for Bayside students, and asked the board to preserve North Star's curriculum and enrichment opportunities.

publicComments.name: Shonda Stewart
publicComments.summary: As a parent with children at both North Star and Orion, argued that North Star's parent fundraising perpetuates educational inequality, that the school culture is not socioeconomically inclusive, and that outreach to Bayside schools has been inadequate compared to Mandarin immersion community outreach.

publicComments.name: Katie Goetz
publicComments.summary: As a North Star Forward Committee member focused on third grade attrition, argued that enriched programming should be available to all RCSD students regardless of testing, since no student is more in need of enrichment than any other, and urged the board to pursue equity and justice for all students.

publicComments.name: Nicole Kowaki
publicComments.summary: Reading a condensed letter co-signed by 20 district parents, cited stark demographic disparities between North Star and the broader district to argue that North Star as currently constituted amounts to publicly funded education for the affluent, and urged the board to support the equitable solutions proposed by the North Star Forward Committee.

publicComments.name: Daryl Norcott
publicComments.summary: As a Clifford parent, argued that North Star inherently widens the achievement gap, that standardized testing is racially biased, that children who don't get in feel stigmatized, and that the enrichment model should be brought to students at their neighborhood schools rather than concentrating resources at one location.

publicComments.name: Heidi von Brielle
publicComments.summary: Raised environmental concerns about the carbon footprint of families driving to North Star, argued that the culture of school transfers undermines neighborhood school funding and volunteerism, and urged the board to implement options that would end the 'musical chairs' dynamic, including possibly a Bayside hub.

publicComments.name: Mike Beebe
publicComments.summary: As a North Star third-grade parent who also has children in the district, urged the board to carefully examine whether the issue is one of admissions process or information and logistics, cautioning against a hard percent-admit model before exhausting outreach and transportation solutions.

publicComments.name: Ann Hinesek
publicComments.summary: As a North Star Forward Committee member, highlighted bringing the Renzulli method to all schools and equalizing PTO fundraising distribution as key equity recommendations, and expressed personal support for changing the grade configuration, adding Spanish-speaking staff, capping school admittance, and possibly moving North Star to the Bayside.
